summary: The candidate adds an atomic deleted-client tombstone and rejects tombstoned IDs in generic wildcard and local-network resolution while exact active registrations still take precedence. Tests cover both re-resolution paths and preserve development-origin behavior for active clients, and the confirmation text reflects the deletion effect.

evidence: `deleteManagedClient` writes `deletedManagedClientKey(record.clientId)` in the same atomic commit that deletes the managed registration in `src/auth_store.ts` lines 476-483.

`effectiveClient` reads that tombstone and passes the disabled ID to `resolveClient`, whose disabled check blocks wildcard and local-network generic fallback while preserving exact registrations in `src/http.ts` lines 133-140 and `src/auth_config.ts` lines 222-235.
`tests/bun_test.ts` lines 37-97 exercise both wildcard and local-network re-resolution after deletion and verify active registered clients retain local development-origin behavior.
`public/admin_projects.js` lines 529-533 updates the deletion confirmation to include wildcard and local development origins.
